Visa’s Stablecoin Settlement Volume Surpasses $25 Billion Annualized, Up 10x YoY Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said during the company’s latest earnings call that its stablecoin settlement volume has surpassed $25 billion on an annualized basis, up 10x year-over-year. Visa now supports 10 blockchains across all five global regions. Visa also has more than 225 stablecoin-linked card programs, up over 70% year-over-year, with transaction volume growing more than 150% across approximately 5 million cards in over 50 countries. Its Visa Stablecoin Platform is now available in the U.S., Mexico, Puerto Rico, Colombia, Switzerland, and the U.K., with a pipeline of more than 300 potential partners. — link

Chinese Payments Giant Alipay Denies Supporting Crypto Trading via Third-Party Platforms Chinese payments giant Alipay stated that it does not support cryptocurrency trading or related services, adding that claims suggesting Alipay enables crypto purchases through third-party platforms are false and unauthorized. The statement came after P2P trading platform Peer announced beta support for buying and selling USDC using CNY payments via Alipay. Alipay also warned users to exercise caution to protect their funds and account security. — link

Allium, Blockchain Data Provider Serving Visa, Stripe and Coinbase, Discloses Security Breach Blockchain data infrastructure provider Allium disclosed that it detected unauthorized access to certain systems on October 25. The company has notified affected customers and engaged an independent cybersecurity firm to investigate. Its core services, including the Allium App, Explorer, and Explorer APIs, are back online, although some features remain unavailable. Allium has not disclosed the full scope of the incident. The company raised $40 million in Series B funding in June and serves clients including Visa, Stripe, and Coinbase. — link

Tether Blacklists Dozens of TRON Addresses Holding Approximately $27 Million in USDT According to TrustSniffer, Tether blacklisted at least 33 addresses on the TRON network on October 28. The addresses held approximately $27 million in USDT at the time they were flagged, with the largest individual address holding around $7.8 million. The figures are based on monitored address balances and do not necessarily represent the exact amount frozen at execution. Tether has not publicly disclosed the reasons for the coordinated blacklisting activity. — link
